title: Landing pages and CRO
purpose: When I am paying for clicks that do not buy, open Landing pages and CRO to find where the page loses them, fix that first, and prove each change with a real result.
fires: The CRO agency's self-graded monthly deck, the redesign every 2 years, the designer's gut, the Sunday night of session recordings, and tests called on a good Tuesday.
not_for: A store with fewer than about 100 orders a month and little paid traffic, where talking to 5 buyers and fixing the obvious beats any page testing.

jobs.job: When I am paying for clicks that do not buy, tell me the one step where most shoppers drop and what it costs me, so I fix that first instead of redesigning everything
jobs.circumstance: Month end; ad costs are up, conversion is 1.4 percent, and the agency wants to redesign the home page

progress.functional: the step losing the most money, with the dollars at stake and the likely causes
progress.emotional: stop the feeling of guessing at a big, invisible leak
progress.social: walk into the agency meeting with a number, not an opinion

jobs.hire_today: a CRO agency audit, an analyst, or a redesign on gut
jobs.fire: the gut redesign and the generic audit deck

forces.push: ad costs rise every quarter and nobody knows where buyers drop
forces.pull: one step named, with its cost per month and what shoppers do there
forces.anxiety: what if the numbers are wrong because tracking is broken

watch.metric: step rates: product view to cart, cart to checkout, checkout to order, mobile, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: cart to checkout is 38 percent, far below the other steps. After: fixed first; 46 percent within 30 days.
jobs.not_for: a store with under about 100 orders a month, where talking to 5 buyers finds the leak faster than any funnel

jobs.job: When a shopper taps an ad that promises '3 for $30, free returns' and lands on a page that says something else, make the page keep the ad's promise, so I do not pay for a click that leaves feeling tricked
jobs.circumstance: Monday review; the top ad has a 71 percent bounce and its page never mentions the offer

progress.functional: the price, offer, guarantee and words on the page match the ad all the way to checkout
progress.emotional: stop the sinking feeling of paying for clicks that leave in 3 seconds
progress.social: end the blame game between the media buyer and the designer

jobs.hire_today: the media buyer and the designer checking by eye, rarely together
jobs.fire: the blame game and the eyeball check

forces.push: bounce is 71 percent on the top ad's page
forces.pull: each live ad traced to its page and cart, with every broken promise named
forces.habit: ads and pages are made by different people
forces.anxiety: what if matching every ad means building 20 pages

jobs.little_hire: every new ad batch, and every Monday

watch.metric: bounce rate on pages that paid social ads land on, mobile, 7 days
watch.source: GA4 landing pages by source, with Meta ads

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the top ad promises free shipping and the page does not; bounce 71 percent. After: offer matched; bounce 58 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store that runs no paid ads and gets most visits from search and email

jobs.job: When a shopper lands on a product page on a phone and does not scroll, show the price, proof, size picker, delivery and buy button on the first screen, so I do not lose them before they decide
jobs.circumstance: Most paid traffic is on phones, and the top product page hides reviews and delivery below the fold

progress.functional: the 5 things a phone shopper needs to decide are on the first screen

jobs.hire_today: a designer or agency judging by eye on a big screen

forces.push: mobile add to cart is 6.1 percent and flat for months
forces.pull: a phone-size check of each top page, with what is missing
forces.anxiety: what if a crowded first screen looks cheap

jobs.little_hire: each new product page, and each theme change

watch.metric: product page add to cart rate, mobile, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: reviews and delivery below the fold; add to cart 6.1 percent. After: all 5 visible; 7.4 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store where most buyers shop on desktop, such as some B2B or high-price stores

jobs.job: When conversion drops overnight, tell me whether it is the page, the traffic mix or broken tracking before anyone redesigns, so I fix the real cause
jobs.circumstance: Tuesday morning; conversion fell from 1.6 to 1.1 percent and the agency is already sketching a new page

progress.functional: the cause named: a traffic source, a device, a broken step or tracking
progress.social: stop the agency spending on the wrong fix

jobs.hire_today: the agency's guess, or a redesign

forces.push: a bad day turns into a costly project
forces.pull: a quick split by source, device and step before any change
forces.anxiety: what if it is all of them at once

jobs.little_hire: whenever conversion moves more than a set amount

watch.metric: days from a conversion drop to its cause being named
watch.source: Shopify and GA4 by source, device and step

drives.metric: conversion rate, 7 days, against the 28 day average

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 3 week redesign after a drop that turned out to be a tracking fault. After: the cause named in 1 day.
jobs.not_for: a store whose daily orders are too few for a daily swing to mean anything

jobs.job: When the same pre-sale question fills the inbox, help me answer it on the page in the customer's own words, so I get fewer tickets and more buyers
jobs.circumstance: 'Will it fit wide feet' drives 1 in 4 pre-sale tickets, and the page says nothing about it

progress.functional: the top doubts answered on the page, where the shopper has them
progress.social: shoppers feel understood before they buy

jobs.hire_today: customer service answering one by one; the copywriter never sees the tickets
jobs.fire: the gap between the support inbox and the page

forces.push: the same question costs support time and lost sales every day
forces.pull: the top 3 doubts from tickets and reviews, each with a place on the page
forces.habit: support and copy do not talk
forces.anxiety: what if naming a doubt plants it in the shopper's head

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and each time a new product launches

watch.metric: pre-sale questions, tickets per 1,000 product page sessions, 30 days

drives.metric: product page add to cart rate, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 'will it fit wide feet' is 1 in 4 pre-sale tickets. After: answered by the size picker; those tickets fall by half.
jobs.not_for: a store with almost no pre-sale questions or reviews to learn from

jobs.job: When a clear fix waits weeks for a test slot, tell me to ship it now, so I do not lose a month of sales to a broken button
jobs.circumstance: A broken size picker on mobile waits 3 weeks behind the agency's test calendar

progress.functional: clear repairs ship at once; tests are kept for real questions
progress.emotional: stop the frustration of watching a known fault run

jobs.hire_today: the agency's test calendar, or the founder's call
jobs.fire: the rule that every change must be tested

forces.push: a broken size picker cost 3 weeks of mobile sales
forces.pull: a plain call: ship, test, or skip, with the reason
forces.anxiety: what if a 'clear' fix actually hurts sales

watch.metric: days from finding a clear fix to shipping it

drives.metric: product page add to cart rate, mobile, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a broken size picker waited 3 weeks. After: clear fixes ship within 3 days.
jobs.not_for: a store with a developer who already ships repairs the same day

jobs.job: When a test is called a winner after 5 days, tell me if the result is real, so I do not roll out a win that fades or lowers sales
jobs.circumstance: The agency calls a win on Friday after a sale weekend, with the split between versions uneven

progress.functional: a plain yes or no on each call, with why: sample, full weeks, even split, clean tracking
progress.social: hold the agency to a standard it cannot argue with

jobs.hire_today: the testing tool's green badge, or the agency's call
jobs.fire: calling tests on a good day

forces.push: 3 of the last 5 wins were called in under a week and faded
forces.pull: each test checked against its own plan before it is called
forces.anxiety: what if waiting costs us the gains

watch.metric: tests called only after the planned sample, full weeks and an even split, share

drives.metric: shipped winners still beating the old version at 60 days, share

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of the last 5 wins called in under a week. After: every call follows the plan; 4 of 5 winners hold.
jobs.not_for: a store too small to run tests at all; it should ship clear fixes instead

jobs.job: When shoppers reach checkout and see shipping for the first time, show the full cost and delivery date earlier, so I do not lose them to a surprise at the last step
jobs.circumstance: 29 percent of checkouts stop at the shipping step

progress.functional: the full cost and a delivery date shown on the product page and in the cart
progress.social: shoppers feel they were told the truth up front

jobs.hire_today: nothing, or the theme default
jobs.fire: the surprise at the last step

forces.push: shipping cost is the top reason shoppers give for leaving
forces.pull: cost and date shown where the shopper decides
forces.anxiety: what if showing shipping early scares off more people

jobs.little_hire: each quarter, and when rates change

watch.metric: checkout abandonment at the shipping step, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 29 percent stop at the shipping step. After: 21 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store with free shipping on every order and dates shown already

jobs.job: When the CRO agency sends its monthly report, tell me what their work actually added in profit, so I know whether the retainer pays for itself
jobs.circumstance: Retainer renewal; the report lists 12 tests and 9 'wins', but revenue looks the same

progress.functional: the net profit added by shipped changes, measured against a held-back group or a clean before and after
progress.social: hold the agency to account with a number it accepts

jobs.hire_today: the agency's own report

forces.push: a $6,000 a month retainer with no clear return
forces.pull: one number: profit added, with how it was measured
forces.anxiety: what if it shows my call to hire them was wrong

watch.metric: profit per visitor on changed pages against a held-back group, 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 9 claimed wins that add up to +40 percent. After: a measured +6 percent profit per visitor, worth about $5,000 a month.
jobs.not_for: a store that runs its own tests with no agency

jobs.job: When the email popup, the chat bubble and the cookie bar all cover the buy button on a phone, stop our own apps getting in the shopper's way, so I let them buy what they came for
jobs.circumstance: Three apps installed by three people; the popup fires at 2 seconds and covers add to cart

progress.functional: no widget covers the buy button or fires before the shopper has looked
progress.emotional: stop the irritation of fighting our own site

jobs.hire_today: nothing; each app is set up alone

forces.push: shoppers close the page instead of the popup
forces.pull: a list of what covers what on each template, with a fix
forces.habit: the popup grows the email list
forces.anxiety: what if the email list stops growing

jobs.little_hire: after any app install, and monthly

watch.metric: mobile add to cart rate on pages with a popup or widget, 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the popup fires at 2 seconds and covers the button. After: it waits for exit intent; add to cart from 5.8 to 6.4 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store with no popups, chat or banners

jobs.job: When mobile converts at half the rate of desktop, find what breaks on the phones our buyers actually use, so I stop losing most of my traffic
jobs.circumstance: Mobile converts at 1.1 percent and desktop at 2.6 percent, and 80 percent of visits are on phones

progress.functional: each key page checked on the phones and screen sizes in our own traffic

jobs.hire_today: a designer or developer checking on their own phone

forces.push: most visits come from the worst-converting device
forces.pull: the faults listed by page and phone size
forces.habit: it looks fine on my phone
forces.anxiety: what if the gap is just normal and not worth fixing

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and before sending traffic to any new page

watch.metric: gap between mobile and desktop conversion rate, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: mobile 1.1 percent, desktop 2.6 percent. After: the gap cut by a third within 60 days.
jobs.not_for: a store whose buyers are mostly on desktop

jobs.job: When a page promises 'ships in 24 hours' or 'free returns' and operations cannot deliver it, catch the gap, so I stop creating angry buyers
jobs.circumstance: The page says 'ships in 24 hours'; the warehouse has been taking 3 days for a month

progress.functional: every promise on the page matches what operations deliver today
progress.emotional: stop the guilt of promising what we cannot keep

jobs.hire_today: nothing; found in tickets and bad reviews

forces.push: shipping-time complaints and 2 star reviews
forces.pull: a list of page promises checked against real ship times and policies
forces.habit: the copy was right when it was written
forces.anxiety: what if the honest promise sells less

watch.metric: page promises that do not match current ship times or policy, count
watch.source: site pages checked against Shopify fulfilment times

drives.metric: tickets about a broken delivery or returns promise, per 100 orders, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 pages promise 24 hour shipping against a 3 day average. After: 0 mismatches; the promise updated the week ship times change.
jobs.not_for: a store with no delivery or returns promises on its pages

jobs.job: When a proposed redesign lands in my inbox, tell me what it is likely to do to sales and what it risks, so I do not spend $30,000 on a new look that sells less
jobs.circumstance: An agency quote for a full redesign sits in the inbox, and the current site sells fine

progress.functional: a view of what is broken against what is just old, and a lower-risk path
progress.social: push back on the agency with facts

jobs.hire_today: the agency's pitch and gut
jobs.fire: the pitch deck as the only input

forces.push: redesigns often drop conversion for months
forces.pull: the specific fixes, ranked, in place of a rebuild
forces.anxiety: what if we look dated to shoppers

watch.metric: conversion rate, 30 days before and after any major page change

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a $30,000 redesign pitch. After: 6 targeted fixes for $4,000; conversion up 0.2 points.
jobs.not_for: a store whose site is truly broken or moving platform, where a rebuild is needed anyway

jobs.job: When shoppers are not sure which size to pick, help them choose right on the page, so I get fewer orders back for fit
jobs.circumstance: Wrong size is the top return reason, and the size guide is a link to a table on another page

jobs.hire_today: a merchandiser's size chart, or nothing

forces.push: 5.2 percent of orders come back for fit
forces.pull: fit help where the choice is made
forces.anxiety: what if fit help slows the shopper down

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and at each new product

watch.metric: returns for size or fit, share of orders, 60 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5.2 percent of orders come back for fit. After: 3.8 percent within 60 days.
jobs.not_for: a store selling products with no size choice

jobs.job: When I spend evenings watching session recordings to see where shoppers struggle, give me the repeated patterns, so I stop losing hours and still see the problem
jobs.circumstance: Sunday night, 50 recordings in, and the founder has seen the same rage tap 6 times but cannot say how common it is

progress.functional: the repeated struggles, with how many shoppers hit each one

jobs.hire_today: the founder watching recordings, or a freelancer's heatmap report

forces.push: hours lost, and still no clear list
forces.pull: the top 5 patterns, each with a count and a clip
forces.habit: I need to see it myself
forces.anxiety: what if the summary misses what I would have seen

watch.metric: hours spent watching recordings per week, and patterns found, count

drives.metric: product page add to cart rate, 30 days

jobs.not_for: a store with no recording tool and no plan to add one

jobs.job: When a shopper hesitates at the size picker or the price, put the proof that answers that doubt right there, so I do not make them scroll to the bottom for reassurance

progress.functional: each doubt has its proof beside it

forces.push: shoppers leave at the moment of doubt
forces.pull: a map of each doubt to its proof and its place on the page
forces.anxiety: what if moving proof clutters the page

watch.metric: product page add to cart rate, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 top doubts with no proof nearby. After: each doubt answered in place; add to cart up 0.6 points.
jobs.not_for: a new store with no reviews or proof yet

jobs.job: When a new ad angle starts winning, help me get a page that continues its story within days, so I do not send that angle to a generic product page

forces.push: the winning ad's conversion is capped by a page that does not match
forces.pull: a page for each winning angle, ready in days
forces.habit: one product page for every ad
forces.anxiety: what if we end up with too many pages to keep up

watch.metric: conversion rate of the winning ad's traffic, 14 days

drives.metric: cost per purchase on that ad, 14 days

jobs.job: When a test or a discount 'wins' on conversion rate, tell me what it did to profit per visitor, so I do not ship a win that loses money

progress.functional: cold traffic lands on a page that explains, warm traffic on the product and buy button

jobs.job: When I do not know why buyers bought and why others left, help me ask them at the moment, so I stop guessing what to fix

progress.functional: short questions after purchase and on exit, with answers grouped

jobs.job: When the loudest test idea always goes first, help me rank the ideas by the money they could make and the evidence behind them, so I run the test most likely to pay
